襲.meaning: On laundry day, a <part>sea serpent</part> bursts out of the harbour and charges the washing lines, grabbing every <part>garment</part> it can reach. Minutes later it's back on its rock, wearing six shirts and a bonnet. Fashion is why it chose to <kanji>attack</kanji>.
襲.on: For its last raid it steals one giant <sound>shoe</sound> and paddles off in it like a boat.
襲.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a lady, as it flops down on her <sound>so</sound>fa to show off the bonnet.

銅.meaning: A town orders a <part>gold</part> statue of its mayor and asks the sculptor to make it look the <part>same</part> as him. Ten years later it rains for a week, and the statue's nose turns green. The sculptor kept the gold and used <kanji>copper</kanji>.
銅.on: Now the bakery sells little mayors made of bread <sound>dough</sound>, green icing nose and all.
銅.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' says a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the fountain, and a <sound>ga</sound>rlic seller throws a <sound>ne</sound>t over the green nose.

賢.meaning: A palace <part>servant</part> must bring the queen a hot <part>shellfish</part> without burning her fingers. She threads a <part>pretzel</part> through the shell's hinge and carries it like a handbag, and the queen eats the handle as a snack. Promote that <kanji>intelligent</kanji> girl.
賢.on: Later she teaches the palace puppies to open their own <sound>ken</sound>nel.
賢.kun: Her pet <sound>ca</sound>rp, a <sound>shee</sound>p and a <sound>ko</sound>ala all line up to learn from her.

凝.meaning: A chef stares at his soup, full of <part>doubt</part>: did he add the salt? He wonders so long that the window frosts over and <part>ice</part> creeps across the bowl. When he finally tastes it, the soup won't pour. It has had time to <kanji>congeal</kanji>.
凝.on: He serves it anyway, sliced into cubes beside a plate of <sound>gyo</sound>za.
凝.kun: His <sound>ko</sound>ala kitchen helper rubs the chef's stiff shoulders.

伴.meaning: A lonely queen uses only one <part>half</part> of her royal <part>coat hook</part>; the other peg stays empty for years. One night a shy gardener hangs his muddy jacket there, next to her cape. The palace gasps, then cheers: the queen has a <kanji>consort</kanji>.
伴.on: At their wedding, the cake is dripping with <sound>hon</sound>ey.
伴.kun: He brings his <sound>to</sound>tem pole, his pet <sound>mo</sound>le and a basket of <sound>na</sound>an along with him.

姓.meaning: A <part>woman</part> labels every plant in her garden. Each new <part>life</part> that sprouts gets a tag, Tomato, Rose, Carrot, and then she adds Smith after it, because they're all family now. Everything in her garden shares her <kanji>surname</kanji>.
姓.on: She keeps the spare name tags locked in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe in the shed.

嫁.meaning: A <part>woman</part> marries a quiet beekeeper and moves into his family's <part>house</part>, where his eleven aunts live. By spring she runs the hives, the kitchen and the aunts. That's how it goes when you <kanji>marry into</kanji> a family.
嫁.on: Her wedding gift to them is a fat orange <sound>ca</sound>rp for the pond.
嫁.kun: Every morning the aunts bring the new bride a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt and a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon.
